analysis:
The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md, adding an 'Unreleased — demanded prefix reuse' section at lines 3-8 of the head side. No source code is supplied, so the described behavior changes can't be inspected. Relevant threat IDs: T-041 and SEC-035 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing, TTFT oracle, SSD at-rest window), and the first-content deadline/budget logic that touches billing and availability.

Changelog claims for the next review pass to verify if source arrives:
(1) Authenticated repeated checkpoints get access to the reserved SSD write share on first local appearance. This could loosen the per-donation gate in SSDPrefixCache.donate and widen the at-rest surface. Check that the 20 GiB pre-write reserve, disk budget, 30-minute TTL and HMAC lookup tags are unchanged, and that 'authenticated' means coordinator-authored cacheSalt scope, not a caller-chosen value.
(2) Capture of one aligned demanded boundary in dense Qwen prompts below the solo stripe may increase the number of durable cache artifacts and the same-account TTFT oracle. This remains inside the accepted SEC-035 scope as long as account scoping is intact.
(3) Reuse of immutable compiled prompt templates in the contract cache must keep per-request isolation of dates, prompt data and proof identity. Cross-tenant leakage through shared template state is a risk.
(4) Reconciling first-content input-token budgets from verified exact counts could affect billing and deadline admission. Counts must come from a renderer identity that matches the serving renderer, and provider-reported recounts must not extend budgets.

The changelog entry alone shows no concrete regression, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated by documentation text. Coverage is limited to the changelog; the source behavior remains unexamined.
